learning_objective: 🎯 Express your views creatively! Learn to structure your thoughts into engaging articles for school magazines and newspapers.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Start with a catchy, relevant heading (Title). Right below it in the center or on the right side, write the By-line ('By [Name given in question]').
Start strong! Hook the reader with a quote, a startling fact, or a question. Clearly state what the article is about.
This is where you explain the topic. Discuss the causes, effects, advantages, disadvantages, and current statistics related to the issue.
Never leave an article hanging. Conclude with a hope, a warning, an appeal, or practical suggestions/solutions.
Use linking words to make your paragraphs flow smoothly (e.g., Firstly, Moreover, Furthermore, Consequently, On the other hand, To sum up).

fun_activity.title: 🧲 The Catchy Title Game
fun_activity.instructions: Topic: Global Warming. Boring title: 'Global Warming'. Catchy titles: 'Our Planet on Fire!' or 'The Heat is On: Fighting Climate Change'. Create a catchy title for 'Mobile Addiction in Teens'.

exam_tips: 📌 Do NOT write articles in bullet points. You must use proper paragraphs.
📌 Always use the name given in the question prompt for the by-line. Don't write your real name.
📌 Keep within the 120-150 word limit. Don't overwrite, it leads to grammatical mistakes.
quick_recap: ⭐ Format: Heading -> By-line -> Intro -> Body -> Conclusion.
⭐ The tone can be formal or slightly informal depending on the topic, but never use slang.
⭐ Quotes or rhetorical questions make excellent beginnings and endings.
